newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork bellies end up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork bellies end up on short covering.

text.p: Short covering prompted by projected lighter hog runs and slaughter kept CME hog and pork belly futures supported at the close, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.800 to 0.325 cent per lb higher with February up most at 75.700 cents. June set a new contract high of 75.400 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.025 to 0.350 cents higher with February up 0.450 at 78.300 cents.

Expectations that hog runs may be hampered by another round of winter weather that started to move through the Midwest reinforced short covering linked to a lighter-than- expected hog run Friday, traders said.

Friday's Iowa-Minnesota receipts totaled 92,000 head below the 105,000 estimate and Monday's estimated receipts at 95,000 head were well under the year-ago level of 120,000 head. The light runs came despite warmer weather over the weekend and could indicate that hog numbers are down and marketings current, traders said.
"It makes you nervous when the weather moderates and you still don't get the hogs," one trader said.
The latest CME lean hog index was lower, but the February contract is already under the index which also lent support, they said.
The light runs, however, and subsequent lighter kills may only be due to muddy road conditions and slack packer demand because cutouts are $3 per cwt negative, one analyst said.

"The hogs are there, its just that the packer doesn't want them plus the fact that when we hit 60 degrees back here (Iowa) there was a lot of mud around these (hog) places. Some of these big pork producers live on dirt roads," said Dave Maher from Securities Corporation of Iowa.
Rand Financials bought February through June early while ADM Investor Services spread April/February. Lind-Waldock sold February and E.D.&F. Man sold April late, pit sources said.
In hog options, ADM, Iowa Grain and Rosenthal Collins sold February 76 puts and calls, pit sources added.
The expected ligher hog kills prompted short covering in pork bellies despite further weakness in cash bellies.
USDA quoted seedless bellies $1 lower at midday, with fresh skin-on bellies weighing 12 to 14 lbs at $70.00 per cwt.
"With the lower kill, that's fewer bellies for the freezer," Maher said.
However, rolling of longs into March continued to limit the gain in February. Rosenthal Collins and LFG bought February against the spreads, pit sources said.
